newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Analysts hope for more GUS Glasnost.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Analysts hope for more GUS Glasnost.

text.p: First half results from Great Universal Stores Plc next Thursday will turn the spotlight on the retailer's future plans in the wake of its billion dollar acquisition of U.S. information firm Experian.

The actual figures have been flagged already in a profit warning in October, when the home shopping-to-Burberry group said first half pre-tax profits would be around one percent lower than a year ago due to a fall in demand in home shopping.
GUS's pretax profits for the six months to September 30, 1995 were 237.5 million stg, versus 226.8 million the year before.
Analysts are forecasting a dividend of about 5.4 pence up from 5.0 pence last time.

The Experian deal marked a break with the past for the secretive and deeply conservative retailer. Analysts described this as "Glasnost at GUS," which had previously been reluctant to spend its vast cash resources on acquisitions.
"There is expectation of more to come," said one retail analyst. Speculation has focused on a possible flotation of its highly profitable Burberry of demerger of the property arm, they said.
The change of pace followed the arrival of Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale as chairman in August, taking over from his older cousin Lord Wolfson of Marylebone.

Analysts are now eager for more information on strategy, and particularly what plans GUS has for its huge, but sluggish mail order business, which is weighted heavily towards the declining agency sector.

"The Experian deal satisfied people's demand for GUS to use its money for something, but there's still a lot of hidden value in the company," said one retail analyst, who asked not to be identified. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
